2027-02-10.title: First Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Rahab protects the spies of Israel
Salvation is not through the law
2027-02-10.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Latin Catholics begin Lent today with Ash Wednesday.
2027-02-10.verse: But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
theo: Genesis shows us the first thing in creation that God calls “not good”: “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper as his partner.” The man names every animal, but among them “there was not found a helper as his partner.” So God casts him into a deep sleep, takes one of his ribs and builds a woman, and the man wakes to cry out with joy: “This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.” Therefore “a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh”, and they “were both naked, and were not ashamed.” We do not keep the Great Fast alone. In Kerala it has always been a family fast: the whole household gives up meat and fish together, and the evening family prayer becomes a little longer. The calendar notes that weddings are not celebrated from the beginning of the fast until Easter, so that the joy of the wedding feast may wait for the joy of the Resurrection. In many homes, especially in the last weeks, the Puthen Pana of Arnos Pathiri, the old Malayalam poem on the life and Passion of Christ, is sung or read aloud. Today our Latin Catholic neighbours receive their ashes; the Church in Kerala walks through these weeks together.

In the second reading an outsider becomes a believer. Rahab of Jericho hides Joshua's spies on her roof and confesses what she has heard: “The LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below.” She asks for mercy on her household, and the sign of her safety is a crimson cord tied in the window through which she let them down. Matthew later names her among the ancestors of Jesus. Paul says something similar: “it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous in God's sight, but the doers of the law who will be justified.” Even those without the law can “show that what the law requires is written on their hearts”, while those who know the law may fail to live it: “you, then, that teach others, will you not teach yourself?” Jesus applies this to prayer. Do not pray to be seen. “Go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret.” Do not “heap up empty phrases”, “for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.” The Great Fast invites us into that inner room, where no one is watching except the Father who loves us.
outline: Ask: where is your inner room, the place where you meet God alone?
Point 1 · Not good to be alone
A family fast, a family prayer.
Point 2 · A crimson cord in the window
Rahab's faith; doers, not only hearers.
Prayer seen only by the Father.
“Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
live: Spend ten minutes each day of this week in silent prayer, alone, with your phone outside the room.
Add one Gospel passage or one decade of the Rosary to your evening family prayer for the whole Great Fast.
2027-02-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you said it is not good for us to be alone, and you gave us families to walk with us. Make our homes places of prayer during this Great Fast. Give us Rahab's faith, make us doers of your word and not hearers only, and lead each of us into the inner room where the Father sees in secret. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we pray together as one family, and in the silence after Communion each of us enters the inner room with Christ.

quick: It is not good to be alone: we keep the fast as families.
Rahab believed and was saved; be a doer of the word.
Pray in secret; the Father sees and knows what you need.
2027-02-10.action: Pray for ten minutes today in a quiet room with the door shut.
2027-02-10.question: Do I pray to be seen, or to be with the Father?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you pray, you do not need to show off or use lots of words. Go to a quiet place, shut the door, and talk to your Father in heaven. He already knows what you need, and he loves to hear you!
family.intention: We pray for married couples and for families keeping the Great Fast together.
family.ask: Ask: “Where in our home can we make a quiet corner for prayer?”

illus: A young couple in Kottayam, both working long shifts, agreed at the start of the Great Fast to switch off their phones at nine each night and pray together for ten minutes. The first evenings were awkward; the silence felt long. By Easter the wife said they had talked to each other more in those seven weeks than in the whole year before. The husband said: we went into the room to talk to God, and we found each other there too.

pm.open: Father in heaven, we have come into your presence. You see in secret and you know what we need. Hear us. Amen.
share: It is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). How can my family keep this fast together?
The LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below (Joshua 2:11). What does Rahab's faith teach me?
Pray to your Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). Do I have an inner room for prayer?
interc: For the Church in Kerala, of every tradition, walking through the Lenten season together.
For married couples, that they may pray together.
For those who are lonely, especially the elderly living alone.
For those who have never learned to pray.
For our group, that our prayer may be sincere.
pm.close: Father, you see in secret and know our needs before we ask. Draw us into prayer that is honest and simple, and bless our families in this holy fast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the first thing in creation that God calls not good is loneliness: it is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). So God gives the man a partner, and the two become one flesh. We do not keep the Great Fast alone. We keep it as families, as a parish, as one Church.

Rahab, a woman of Jericho, hears what God has done and believes: the LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below (Joshua 2:11). She ties a crimson cord in her window and is saved with her family. Paul reminds us that God wants doers of his word, not only hearers.

And Jesus teaches us how to pray: not to be seen, not with many words, but in the inner room. Go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). The Father knows what we need before we ask.
This Great Fast, let us find our inner room, and let our families pray together each evening. Then the Father who sees in secret will reward us. Amen.
kids: Children, you can talk to God anywhere, even in a quiet corner of your room. Shut the door, close your eyes and tell him what is in your heart. He is listening!

intro: Theme: “Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
The gift of companionship, Rahab's faith, and the inner room of prayer.

q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points.apply: Plan with your family one shared Lenten practice and keep it until Easter.

points.h: A crimson cord in the window
q: She said, “According to your words, so be it.” She sent them away and they departed. Then she tied the crimson cord in the window.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.
points.apply: Put into practice today one word of Scripture you already know well.

q: O LORD, you have searched me and known me.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Make a quiet prayer corner at home this week.

concl: God made us for communion: with one another, and above all with him.
Keep the fast together, live the word you hear, and meet the Father in secret.
2027-02-10.resolve: Pray ten minutes in silence every day of this week.
